claude.rationale: On gap_45: the customer-facing weight-management operation (T4) did not move out of its vehicles — only the 49% equity crossed, and the Hong Kong entity and PRC WFOE that produce/deliver the service "remained in place" (§2.1, §Recitals A), so product and its operating processes stayed together within the same continuing WFOE; no product-vs-process mismatch at closing. On gap_56: the operational/governance layer was re-set at closing — the founding JV agreement and the DAPM services agreement terminated (§3.3(b),(c),(d)) — while the counterparty's directors, supervisors, and management delivered resignation letters and were replaced (§3.2(a)(iii)-(v)); processes were re-engineered/severed while the counterparty's people were exited rather than transferred, and the filing records "no transitional-services, operating, or shared-services agreement carrying Danone-provided support forward past Closing," so the gap is not contractually mitigated.

gemini.rationale: The transaction transferred the remaining equity of the joint venture to Weight Watchers, but Danone's appointed directors and management personnel resigned at closing (T6 subset). Additionally, the pre-existing services agreement from Danone was terminated without a replacement transition services agreement, creating a structural gap between the continuing operations and the departing management/support.

grok.rationale: The slice establishes that the customer-facing China weight-management operation remained inside the same HK entity and PRC WFOE whose 49% equity crossed to WW, with no structural separation of product from the entity’s own delivery processes at closing (gap_45=0). Danone-appointed directors/supervisors/management resigned at Closing in tandem with termination of the DAPM–WFOE services agreement and the JV agreement, so the counterparty process exit and people exit were aligned rather than a processes-without-organization mismatch (gap_56=0); the filing records no TSA bridging any shared substrate.
